solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An attitude taken by mum twitching is serving as a warning

parts.note: the article as a single letter
a pose is a bodily attitude or stance
a familiar word for mother
a tic is an involuntary twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: A mother's nervous twitch and odd stance are a signal of something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitching' reads as an adjective on mum, but it is a noun here, the nervous spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use the term for bright colouring that tells predators an animal is poisonous or distasteful.

clue.text: Figure that would be easy if one were positive

indicators.note: asks us to imagine a letter standing for 'one' in the slot held by the letter for 'positive', a swap of one for the other

parts.note: easy means simple, straightforward
the Roman numeral for one
P is the abbreviation for positive

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a sum would be easy if a number were positive.
explanation.walkthrough: Put I where the P of SIMPLE stands and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech, a comparison using 'like' or 'as'.

clue.text: Worker on fire, a Belgian nationalist

parts.note: something on fire is flaming
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A worker in flames is described, as if a Belgian activist had set himself alight.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker comes first in the clue but last in the answer: 'on' places it after the fire word.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a supporter of Flemish rights and language in Belgium, the Flemish nationalist movement.

clue.text: The French m-mate turned up in a flap once

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: the masculine French definite article
a mate is a pal, and the stammered m-mate asks for a stammered first letter

explanation.surface: A stammering Frenchman's mate gets into a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'm-mate' is a stutter: the synonym repeats its first letter as well. This is an old spelling, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back flap on a coat front; this doubled-P form is obsolete spelling.

clue.text: A female getting compliment finally as a "dish"?

parts.note: taken as written
the female pronoun

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of compliment

explanation.surface: An attractive woman, a 'dish', is paid a compliment.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around dish warn that it is not the slang for an attractive person but a literal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England an ashet is a large serving plate, especially for a joint of meat.

clue.text: The fellow wanting original food and drink

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and original points to the opening letter as the one lost

parts.note: meat is an old word for food in general
the word The, which once its head is gone leaves the pronoun for a fellow

explanation.surface: A man goes without a proper meal of food and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T of The and what remains is HE, which is also 'the fellow'. The food piece comes after it in the clue but first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete word for mead, the fermented honey drink, spelt variously meath or meathe.

clue.text: What will appear in spring? Answer: Scottish bulbs

indicators.note: what appears within a word is a run of letters already sitting inside it

parts.note: the closing three letters lie inside the word
ans. is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A gardening quiz: what comes up in spring? The answer is bulbs from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Answer:' set up a quiz, but 'Answer' is just the abbreviation tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingans is Scots dialect for onions, which are bulbs.

clue.text: Black liquid in which you'll see rodent sink after falling over

indicators.note: falling over turns a thing upside down, which in a down entry means read from the bottom

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: A rat falls into a pool of black liquid and sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas tar is the black coal tar left over from making coal gas.

clue.text: Dietician troubled with iodine lacking as element

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so its letters are stirred into a new order
lacking means going without, so the chemical symbol is removed

parts.note: taken as written
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A dietician worries about a diet low in iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's element is the dietary mineral iodine, but the answer is a different element entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Any of the actinide series, the radioactive elements from actinium to lawrencium, is an element.

clue.text: Radioactive element that was out having been lifted

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means raised from bottom to top, so read upwards

parts.note: out means not in

explanation.surface: A radioactive element has been removed, lifted out of the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was' marks the definition as a former name.
explanation.definitionFit: Niton was the early name for radon, the radioactive noble gas, before the modern name was adopted.

clue.text: Holy Fathers? Toads!

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, holy
pas are fathers, plural of pa

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at the clergy: Holy Fathers? Toads!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy Fathers' looks like one phrase for popes, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipa is the Surinam toad, which carries its eggs in pits on its back.

clue.text: Acid in can I spilt

indicators.note: spilt contents scatter, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to spilling acid stored in a can.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin is nicotinic acid, one of the B vitamins.

clue.text: Old cleaner, ugly old woman, with yen for eating raw flesh

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a mop is a cleaning tool
a hag is an ugly old woman
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency, added with

explanation.surface: An old charwoman and a hag share a craving for raw meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen for' reads as a craving, but yen is the currency letter and 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Omophagy, from Greek omos raw and phagein to eat, is the practice of devouring uncooked meat.

clue.text: Special cuisine I avoided — time for fasting — that can't be eaten!

indicators.note: something special is made out of the ordinary, so its letters are remade
avoided means left out, so the single letter named is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: During a fast someone avoided fancy cooking, finding it inedible.
explanation.definitionFit: Esculent means edible, so its negative describes food unfit for eating.

clue.text: A little to eat in course at Oxford — take a seat devouring it

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing whole, so one piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: to take a seat is to sit
Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a well-known Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: An Oxford student grabs a snack between lectures while sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a meal course, but it is a degree course. 'It' refers back to that course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sippet is a small piece of toast or bread dipped in soup or gravy, a morsel.

clue.text: Behaviour of clique ousting leader

indicators.note: to oust a leader is to remove the one at the front

parts.note: a faction is a clique within a group

explanation.surface: The conduct of a party faction plotting to remove its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Action can mean conduct or behaviour, as in judging someone by their actions.

clue.text: Home all confused — power to be installed in space where light enters

indicators.note: installing something puts it inside another thing
confused letters are muddled into another order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A house in chaos as the electricity is put in, leaving a gap for light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamphole is a shaft in a sewer through which a lamp is lowered for inspection, an opening for light.

clue.text: I have a significant nap, getting criticised endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone takes a long snooze and gets told off without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is not a snooze but the raised pile on fabric; the definition speaks as the cloth itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Panne is a velvet with a long pile pressed flat, so a noticeable nap is its defining trait.

clue.text: Bit of cereal that is served with breakfast first?

indicators.note: says which piece goes in front when the two are put together

parts.note: breakfast is a meal
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A morning question about what comes with the cereal served at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A mealie is an ear of maize in South Africa, a single bit of the cereal crop.

clue.text: Stimulant that's chewed by American star

parts.note: siri is betel, the leaf chewed as a stimulant
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American is chewing a stimulant, like a gum-chewing film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewed by' looks like a container instruction but merely describes the betel; 'by' then joins the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: Jolly lot with funny tale about band

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer letters wrap the other piece
something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, and the whole corps is RM

explanation.surface: A cheerful group of musicians telling a comic story about a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly lot' reads as a cheerful crowd, but jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, so the lot is the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn around the arm.

clue.text: Tirade from Scottish girl slightly confused inside

indicators.note: only a little mixing-up, and only in the middle, so just the interior letters change places

parts.note: lassie is the Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: A flustered Scottish girl launches into a rant.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters stay put; just the S and I in the middle swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A laisse is a stanza or long verse paragraph of Old French epic, also used for a tirade or long speech.

clue.text: Eating stews — this being one of them?

definitions.text: Eating stews — this being one of them?

indicators.note: stewing cooks things into a mixture, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner tucking into stews wonders whether this dish is one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the anagram's result is itself one of the stews being eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew, named after the conical pot it is made in.

clue.text: Language of top commander gets kept within bounds

indicators.note: inside the boundaries means enclosed by the outer piece

parts.note: C-in-C, Commander in Chief
had means kept or held, as in had a dog

explanation.surface: The supreme commander's language is kept in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Chadic is a branch of Afro-Asiatic languages spoken around Lake Chad, including Hausa.

clue.text: Poison containing copper, mostly uncommon one

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare means uncommon
a means one

explanation.surface: A rare poison laced with copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' looks like a container signal, but the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Curara is a variant of curare, the South American arrow poison that paralyses muscles.

clue.text: Suddenly no longer at rest, being agitated

definitions.note: 'no longer' marks the word as obsolete

indicators.note: agitated things are shaken up, so the letters are stirred

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who was resting is suddenly roused and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer at rest' looks like one phrase, but 'no longer' belongs to the definition as an obsolete tag.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Spenserian adverb meaning abruptly or all at once, a form of astart.

clue.text: I grant this eye problem could be irritating — and is!

indicators.note: could be suggests one set of letters might be rearranged into another
the clue's equation balances once the letters on its first side are taken away from the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A patient concedes that their eye condition could be irritating, and indeed is.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: I + GRANT + the answer has the same letters as IRRITATING + IS, so take I GRANT out of those and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the iris, a painful condition of the eye.

clue.text: Best characters, first and last, producing a gem

parts.note: top means best
the first and last characters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The finest letters, first to last, make up a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, often yellow or golden.

clue.text: Boorish Aussie is scoffer putting maiden off

indicators.note: putting off means removing, here the single cricket letter

parts.note: one who scoffs is a mocker
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A crude Australian mocks people and turns off a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocker is Australian slang for a loud, uncultured Australian man.

clue.text: What's consumed by this enormous foreign gentleman

indicators.note: what is eaten up by the following words is sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A huge visiting gentleman eats a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish title for a man, the equivalent of Mr or sir.

clue.text: One prominent feature introducing grand Chinese book

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a prominent chin is a common facial feature
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A notable feature introduces a grand Chinese volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The I Ching, or Book of Changes, is an ancient Chinese classic used for divination.

clue.text: High Street activity that is limited about to come to the fore?

indicators.note: says that one piece is to be placed at the front of the other

parts.note: re means about, concerning
in law, tail describes an estate limited to particular heirs

explanation.surface: Shops on the main street face limited trade and are about to come forward.
explanation.walkthrough: TAIL here is the legal adjective, as in 'fee tail', an inheritance limited to certain heirs. A High Street is a British town's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail, selling goods to the public in shops, is the business of the main shopping street.

clue.text: Small instrument hurt patient taking drug

indicators.note: something hurt is damaged, so its letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An injured patient is being given medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianette is a small upright piano, a compact keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Phone member of family being a bit "crabby"?

parts.note: tel. is the abbreviation for telephone
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: A relative is a bit grumpy on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around crabby flag that it means belonging to a crab or crustacean, not bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: The telson is the last tail segment of a crustacean such as a lobster or crab.

clue.text: Plant given gold fastener

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a pin is a fastener

explanation.surface: A plant is staked up with a golden clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpin, or orpine, is a sedum, the stonecrop plant also called livelong.

clue.text: Mineral found in ditch, source of energy brought into yard

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside, so these letters go within the next piece

parts.note: a garth is an enclosed yard or garden
reen is a dialect word for a drainage ditch

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of energy

explanation.surface: A mineral turns up in a ditch, and a power source is brought into the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Green earth is glauconite or celadonite, a greenish clay mineral used as an artist's pigment.
